messages.subject: Re: MaAsLin questions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Liz - many thanks for getting in touch; I've CCed in the MaAsLin users group to chime in, but my short version would be that it's typically best to use very targeted tests for small sample sizes, making MaAsLin's multivariate model more appropriate for larger / more complicated study designs.  LEfSe was originally designed for cases like that, and more recent methods like MetaStats and PhyloSeq are similarly intended for simpler, smaller designs, if that's the main regime you'll be working in.

Thanks again -
Curtis

On Mon, May 9, 2016 at 3:14 PM, Elizabeth Bent <eb...@uoguelph.ca> wrote:

Is it possible to use MaAsLin to try to pick up associations in smaller data sets (I realize that using small data sets loses statistical power)? Do you give workshops in how to use this tool? I'm a novice at bioinformatics.

messages.subject: Order of metadata variables and results
messages.subject_clean: Order of metadata variables and results
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Why do results change depending on the order at which variables are inputted? From what I can gather looking at the data_log, it seems that the linear models respect the hierarchy of importance as determined by gbm: e.g., if the rel.inf of variable A > B > 0 for OTU1, then lm(OTU1 ~ A + B), which is of course different from OTU1 ~ B + A. Would it make sense/be possible to change the defaults in the optional .R file to run marginal tests, which are independent of variable order? Also, why do variables with a rel.inf close to 0 get included in subsequent lm models?

Many thanks.
